questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four listed treatment modalities for breast cancer?
questions.exp: Treatment modalities for breast cancer: 1. Surgery; 2. Chemotherapy; 3. Radiotherapy (RT); 4. Hormonal therapy (HT). Immunotherapy is not listed. (Book p61)

questions.q: Surgical management of breast cancer is divided into surgery for:
questions.exp: Surgical mx of breast cancer: Sx for breast + Sx for lymph nodes. (Book p61)

questions.q: Surgery for the breast is divided into which two operations?
questions.exp: Sx for breast: BCS vs mastectomy. (Book p61)

questions.q: Overall survival after BCS compared with mastectomy is:
questions.exp: BCS vs mastectomy table: Overall survival = Same. (Book p61)

questions.q: Local recurrence rate after BCS is:
questions.exp: Local recurrence: BCS = 3-4% (Hence RT is mandatory). (Book p61)

questions.q: Why is radiotherapy mandatory after BCS?
questions.exp: BCS local recurrence 3-4%, hence RT is mandatory. (Book p61)

questions.q: Local recurrence rate after mastectomy is:
questions.exp: Local recurrence: mastectomy = 1%. (Book p61)

questions.q: Oncoplasty combines the principles of cancer surgery with:
questions.exp: Oncoplasty: Principles of cancer Sx + Plastic Sx. (Book p61)

questions.q: Volume displacement oncoplasty is used for what breast volume resection?
questions.exp: Volume displacement: 10-15% breast volume resection. (Book p61)

questions.q: Volume replacement oncoplasty is indicated when breast volume resection is:
questions.exp: Volume replacement: ≥15% breast volume resection. (Book p61)

questions.q: BCS with round block technique and BCS with periareolar incision are examples of:
questions.exp: BCS with round block technique / periareolar incision = Volume displacement. (Book p61)

questions.q: Importing tissue (e.g. a flap) to fill a defect after ≥15% breast volume resection is:
questions.exp: ≥15% resection needs volume replacement (flap shown in images). (Book p61)

questions.q: The absolute contraindication for RT (and hence BCS) is:
questions.exp: Absolute C/I for RT: 1. Pregnancy. (Book p62)

questions.q: The absolute technical contraindication for BCS is:
questions.exp: Absolute technical C/I: 1. Multicentric tumors. (Book p62)

questions.q: Relative contraindications for RT include prior RT to chest wall and:
questions.exp: Relative C/I for RT: 2. Prior RT to chest wall; 3. Collagen vascular diseases (SLE, RA). (Book p62)

questions.q: Multifocal tumors, diffuse microcalcifications/DCIS in entire breast, LABC and large tumor : breast ratio are:
questions.exp: Relative technical C/1: multifocal tumors; diffuse microcalcifications/DCIS in entire breast; LABC; large tumor : breast ratio. (Book p62)

questions.q: Multicentric tumors means tumors in:
questions.exp: Diagram: multicentric = tumors in different quadrants (absolute technical C/I). (Book p62)

questions.q: Multifocal tumors means tumors in:
questions.exp: Diagram: multifocal = multiple tumors clustered in one quadrant (relative technical C/I). (Book p62)

questions.q: BCS can still be done in LABC / large tumor : breast ratio after:
questions.exp: BCS can be done post neo adjuvant chemo (LABC, large tumor : breast ratio). (Book p62)

questions.q: BCS amounts to lumpectomy with what margin?
questions.exp: BCS = Lumpectomy with 1 mm margin. (Book p62)

questions.q: Mastectomy means:
opts: Removal of tumor with 1 mm margin
questions.exp: Mastectomy: Removal of entire breast. (Book p63)

questions.q: The incision used for radical mastectomy is:
questions.exp: Radical mastectomy incision: Halstead. (Book p63)

questions.q: The incision used for modified radical mastectomy (MRM) is:
questions.exp: MRM incision: Elliptical Stewart. (Book p63)

questions.q: Structures removed in radical mastectomy include breast, NAC, level 1-3 axillary nodes and:
questions.exp: Radical mastectomy removes: Breast; NAC; Pectoralis major & minor; Level 1,2,3 axillary lymph nodes. (Book p63)

questions.q: In MRM, instead of the pectoral muscles, what is removed?
questions.exp: MRM removes breast, NAC, pectoral fascia, level 1,2,3 axillary lymph nodes (± p. minor). (Book p63)

questions.q: In MRM, when the pectoralis minor is retracted the procedure is called:
questions.exp: ± P. minor: Retracted → Auchincloss. (Book p63)

questions.q: In MRM, when the pectoralis minor is cut the procedures are:
questions.exp: ± P. minor: Cut → Patey, Scanlon. (Book p63)

questions.q: In simple mastectomy:
questions.exp: Simple mastectomy: Breast, NAC, pectoral fascia; lymph nodes NOT removed. (Book p63)

questions.q: NAC removed in all mastectomies stands for:
questions.exp: NAC = Nipple areola complex (removed in radical, MRM and simple mastectomy). (Book p63)

questions.q: The two conservation-type mastectomies illustrated are:
opts: Nipple sparing and skin sparing mastectomy
questions.exp: Images: Nipple sparing mastectomy; Skin sparing mastectomy. (Book p63)

questions.q: The medial boundary of axillary clearance is:
questions.exp: Medial boundary: Halstead ligament. (Book p63)

questions.q: The superior boundary of axillary clearance is:
questions.exp: Superior boundary: Axillary vein. (Book p63)

questions.q: The lateral boundary of axillary clearance is:
questions.exp: Lateral boundary: Thoraco-dorsal pedicle. (Book p63)

questions.q: The inferior boundary of axillary clearance is:
questions.exp: Inferior boundary: Angular vein. (Book p63)

questions.q: During axillary clearance the long thoracic nerve is:
opts: Saved and is not a boundary
questions.exp: Long thoracic nerve: Saved; Not a boundary. (Book p63)

questions.q: Minimum number of lymph nodes removed in axillary clearance:
questions.exp: Minimum 10 lymph nodes removed in axillary clearance. (Book p63)

questions.q: Bleeding after mastectomy is classified as:
questions.exp: Bleeding: Primary, Reactionary, Secondary. (Book p64)

questions.q: The most commonly (m/c) injured nerve in mastectomy/axillary clearance is:
questions.exp: Injury to nerves: Intercostobrachial nerve (m/c). (Book p64)

questions.q: Intercostobrachial nerve injury causes:
questions.exp: Intercostobrachial nerve (m/c) → Numbness & ↓ sensation in axilla. (Book p64)

questions.q: Winging of scapula after axillary clearance is due to injury of:
opts: Long thoracic nerve / Nerve to Santorini / Nerve of Bell
questions.exp: Long thoracic nerve / Nerve to Santorini / Nerve of Bell → winging of scapula. (Book p64)

questions.q: Injury to the thoracodorsal pedicle affects:
questions.exp: Thoracodorsal pedicle → Affects Latissimus dorsi. (Book p64)

questions.q: Injury to the lateral & medial pectoral nerves affects:
questions.exp: Lateral & medial pectoral nerves → affects P. major/minor. (Book p64)

questions.q: Flap necrosis after mastectomy occurs due to:
questions.exp: Flap necrosis (d/t compromised blood supply). (Book p64)

questions.q: The m/c complication of mastectomy is:
questions.exp: Seroma formation: m/c complication. (Book p64)

questions.q: A seroma is:
questions.exp: Seroma: Fluid accumulation beneath the flap. (Book p64)

questions.q: Seroma after mastectomy is prevented by:
questions.exp: Prevention: Romovac suction drain. (Book p64)

questions.q: The Romovac suction drain is removed when output is:
questions.exp: Removed when output < 40 cc/day for a consecutive days. (Book p64)

questions.q: Treatment of seroma includes all EXCEPT:
opts: Do not put the drain again
questions.exp: Rx of seroma: Aspirate under aseptic conditions; Pressure dressing; Do not put the drain again. (Book p64)

questions.q: Post mastectomy/axillary clearance lymphedema is the:
opts: m/c cause of upper limb lymphedema
m/c cause of lower limb lymphedema
questions.exp: m/c cause of upper limb lymphedema. (Book p64)

questions.q: Post mastectomy lymphedema typically develops:
questions.exp: Develops few weeks-months after Sx. (Book p64)

questions.q: Incidence of lymphedema after lymph node clearance is:
questions.exp: Lymph node clearance (5-15%). (Book p64)

questions.q: Factors which ↑ incidence of lymphedema include removal of lymph nodes above the:
questions.exp: ↑ incidence: Removal of lymph nodes above axillary vein; RT to axilla after lymph node clearance. (Book p64)

questions.q: Which factor ↓ the incidence of lymphedema?
opts: Removal of nodes above axillary vein
questions.exp: Factors which ↓ incidence: Sentinel lymph node biopsy. (Book p64)

questions.q: Management of lymphedema includes:
opts: Skin care, lymphedema massages, stockings, exercise
questions.exp: Mx: Skin care; Lymphedema massages; Stockings; Exercise. (Book p65)

questions.q: Long standing lymphedema for 8-10 years can lead to:
questions.exp: Long standing lymphedema for 8-10 years → 2° cancer/Angiosarcoma → Stewart-Treves syndrome. (Book p65)

questions.q: Stewart-Treves syndrome presents with:
questions.exp: Reddish/bluish skin nodules in long standing lymphedema = Stewart-Treves syndrome. (Book p65)

questions.q: First step in investigating a local recurrence is:
questions.exp: Ix: Repeat biopsy to confirm diagnosis. (Book p65)

questions.q: On repeat biopsy of a local recurrence, IHC markers can show change in expression in:
questions.exp: IHC markers (10-15% can show change in IHC expression). (Book p65)

questions.q: Extensive local recurrences covering the chest wall like armour are called:
questions.exp: Extensive local recurrences → Covers chest wall like armour: Cancer en cuirasse. (Book p65)

questions.q: In phantom breast syndrome the patient:
opts: Feels as if breast is still present
questions.exp: Phantom breast syndrome: Patient feels as if breast is still present. (Book p65)

questions.q: Phantom breast syndrome occurs due to:
questions.exp: D/t ICBN entrapment; Pain (+). (Book p65)

questions.q: Reconstructive surgery after mastectomy uses which flaps?
questions.exp: Reconstructive Sx: TRAM & DIEP; Latissimus dorsi flap can also be used. (Book p65)

questions.q: TRAM flap stands for:
questions.exp: TRAM = Transverse rectus abdominus myocutaneous flap. (Book p65)

questions.q: In TRAM flap which tissues are removed?
questions.exp: TRAM: Elliptical incision; Skin, fat, muscle removed. (Book p65)

questions.q: TRAM flap carries ↑ risk of incisional hernia because:
questions.exp: ↑ Risk of incisional hernia (d/t removal of muscle). (Book p65)

questions.q: DIEP flap stands for:
opts: Deep inferior epigastric artery perforator flap
questions.exp: DIEP = Deep inferior epigastric artery perforator flap. (Book p65)

questions.q: DIEP is the best flap because:
questions.exp: DIEP: Skin & fat removed; Best flap: Less abdominal complications (as muscle is not removed). (Book p65)

questions.q: In the surgical management flowchart, a patient with an enlarged lymph node first undergoes:
questions.exp: Patient with enlarged lymph node → Biopsy LN for cancer. (Book p66)

questions.q: If the LN biopsy for cancer is positive (+ve), the next step is:
questions.exp: +ve → Axillary clearance. (Book p66)

questions.q: If the LN biopsy for cancer is negative (−ve), the next step is:
questions.exp: −ve → SLNB. (Book p66)

questions.q: The concept of sentinel lymph node was described by:
questions.exp: Concept described by: Cabana in penile cancer. (Book p66)

questions.q: The sentinel LN is:
opts: First draining lymph node from cancer
questions.exp: Sentinel LN: First draining lymph node from cancer. (Book p66)

questions.q: The sentinel lymph node is most commonly present in:
questions.exp: Most commonly present in level I of axilla. (Book p66)

questions.q: The m/c nerve injured during SLNB is:
questions.exp: m/c nerve injured: ICBN. (Book p66)

questions.q: SLNB is used in all the following cancers EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Cancers where SLNB is used: Malignant melanoma; Breast cancer; Penile cancer; Vulvar carcinoma; Head & neck cancer. (Book p66)

questions.q: In the blue dye technique, the dye is injected where and in what volume?
opts: 1-1.5 cc methylene blue/isosulfan blue, subcutaneous periareolar
1-1.5 cc indigo carmine subdermal over the tumor
questions.exp: 1-1.5 cc methylene blue/isosulfan blue injected in subcutaneous plane in periareolar region. (Book p66)

questions.q: After localising the blue lymph nodes, the next step is:
questions.exp: Localise blue lymph nodes → Frozen section in normal container. (Book p66)

questions.q: If frozen section of the sentinel node is cancer −ve:
opts: Axillary clearance not needed (hence ↓ incidence of lymphedema)
questions.exp: Cancer −ve → Axillary clearance not needed (Hence ↓ incidence of lymphedema). (Book p66)

questions.q: If frozen section of the sentinel node is cancer +ve, the management is:
questions.exp: Cancer +ve → Mx: Axillary clearance. (Book p66)

questions.q: The m/c complication of the blue dye technique is:
questions.exp: Complications: Skin tattooing (m/c). (Book p66)

questions.q: Which of the following is a listed complication of the blue dye technique?
questions.exp: Complications: Skin tattooing (m/c), Anaphylaxis, Bluish discolouration of urine, Skin necrosis. (Book p66)

questions.q: A harmless listed complication of methylene/isosulfan blue seen in the urine is:
questions.exp: Bluish discolouration of urine is a listed complication. (Book p66)

questions.q: In the radionucleotide technique, what is injected in the periareolar region?
questions.exp: Tc99 tagged sulphur colloid injected in periareolar region. (Book p67)

questions.q: Hot nodes (radioactive) in the radionucleotide technique are identified on:
questions.exp: Hot nodes (Radioactive) identified on gamma camera. (Book p67)

questions.q: The best technique for SLNB is:
questions.exp: Best technique: Combination of blue dye + radionucleotide. (Book p67)

questions.q: In the indocyanine green (ICG) technique, what is injected?
questions.exp: ICG + Blue dye injected → Green lymph nodes under filter. (Book p67)

questions.q: The advantage of the ICG technique is:
opts: Nodes seen with naked eye without filter
questions.exp: Advantages: No radiation exposure. (Book p67)

questions.q: The Sentimag technique uses which compound?
questions.exp: Sentimag technique: Ferric oxide compound used. (Book p67)

questions.q: In the Sentimag technique the lymph node is detected on:
questions.exp: LN detected on magnetic scanner. (Book p67)

questions.q: The advantage of the Sentimag technique is:
questions.exp: Advantages: Zero radiation exposure. (Book p67)

units.title: Treatment Modalities & BCS vs Mastectomy
units.sec: Treatment Modalities & BCS vs Mastectomy · p61
units.guide: Four weapons against breast cancer: surgery, chemotherapy, RT and HT. Surgery tackles breast and lymph nodes; for the breast, BCS and mastectomy give the SAME overall survival, but BCS recurs locally 3-4% (hence RT mandatory) versus 1% after mastectomy.

units.title: Oncoplasty: Volume Displacement & Replacement
units.guide: Oncoplasty fuses cancer surgery with plastic surgery: 10-15% breast volume resections are closed by volume displacement (round block, periareolar incisions), while ≥15% resections need volume replacement with imported tissue.

units.title: Contraindications for BCS
units.guide: Absolute bars: pregnancy (RT) and multicentric tumors (technical, different quadrants). Relative: prior chest wall RT and collagen vascular disease (SLE, RA) for RT; multifocal (same quadrant) tumors, diffuse microcalcifications/DCIS, LABC and large tumor:breast ratio technically - the last two become BCS-eligible after neo adjuvant chemo. BCS = lumpectomy with a 1 mm margin.

units.title: Mastectomy Types
units.guide: Radical (Halstead) takes breast, NAC, pectoralis major & minor and level 1-3 nodes; MRM (elliptical Stewart) spares the muscles taking pectoral fascia, ± pectoralis minor retracted (Auchincloss) or cut (Patey, Scanlon); simple mastectomy removes no nodes. Nipple and skin sparing versions conserve the envelope.

units.title: Boundaries of Axillary Clearance
units.guide: Halstead ligament medially, axillary vein above, thoraco-dorsal pedicle laterally and angular vein below; the long thoracic nerve is saved, not a boundary, and at least 10 nodes must come out.

units.title: Complications: Nerves, Seroma & Flap
units.guide: Bleeding runs primary, reactionary, secondary. The intercostobrachial nerve (m/c) loses axillary sensation; long thoracic (Santorini/Bell) wings the scapula; thoracodorsal hits latissimus dorsi; pectoral nerves hit p. major/minor. Seroma, the m/c complication, is prevented by a Romovac drain pulled at <40 cc/day and treated by aseptic aspiration + pressure dressing, never re-inserting the drain.

units.title: Lymphedema & Stewart-Treves
units.guide: Post-mastectomy lymphedema is the m/c cause of upper limb lymphedema, appearing weeks-months later in 5-15% after clearance - worse if nodes above the axillary vein go or axillary RT follows, less with SLNB. Manage with skin care, massage, stockings, exercise; 8-10 years of swelling can breed angiosarcoma (reddish/bluish nodules) = Stewart-Treves syndrome.

units.title: Local Recurrence, Phantom Breast & Reconstruction
units.sec: Local Recurrence, Phantom Breast & Reconstruction · p65
units.guide: Recurrences need repeat biopsy (10-15% change IHC expression) and armour-like spread is cancer en cuirasse; ICBN entrapment causes painful phantom breast. Reconstruction: TRAM takes skin-fat-muscle (incisional hernia risk) while DIEP, the best flap, takes skin-fat only; latissimus dorsi also serves.

units.title: Surgical Mx of Lymph Nodes & SLNB Basics
units.sec: Lymph Node Mx & SLNB Basics · p66
units.guide: Enlarged nodes get biopsy: positive → axillary clearance, negative → SLNB. Cabana described the sentinel node in penile cancer; it is the first draining node, usually level I, and SLNB (m/c nerve injured ICBN) serves melanoma, breast, penile, vulvar and head & neck cancers.

units.title: Blue Dye Technique
units.guide: 1-1.5 cc methylene/isosulfan blue injected subcutaneously periareolarly stains the sentinel node for frozen section: negative spares axillary clearance (less lymphedema), positive mandates it. Watch for skin tattooing (m/c), anaphylaxis, bluish urine and skin necrosis.

units.title: Radionucleotide, ICG & Sentimag Techniques
units.guide: Tc99 sulphur colloid marks hot nodes on gamma camera and combined blue dye + radionucleotide is the best technique; ICG + blue dye shows green nodes under a filter with no radiation, and Sentimag's ferric oxide is read by a magnetic scanner with zero radiation.
